findings.reason: citing extract_vessel_shells would redirect §4 from a parallel extractor to an extension of the existing one, and resolving where the §2 reader lives (artifact_geometry versus scripts/, as the plan's own record disagrees with itself) changes both §1b's scope and §2's imports.
findings.text: §4 builds vessel extraction into extract_geometry from wall.description_2d.vessel.unit[*] annular outline_inner/outline_outer/centreline, but imas-ink already exports extract_vessel_shells (imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:151, re-exported at imas_ink/__init__.py:128 and :259) which iterates wall.description_2d[0].vessel.unit[*] and reads exactly those annular fields plus an outline fallback; the second instance of type is §2, which reads wall/pf_active/magnetics afresh through imas.DBEntry while the plan never cites the existing machine-geometry readers read_artifact_limiter (imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py:671), read_artifact_magnetics (:577), read_artifact_pf_active (:302) and sensor_position_arrays (:647), nor the MachineArtifactGeometryReader (:726) that the plan's own §1 landing comment (c-20261006T0607) names as where "the reader moves onto artifact_geometry in §1b" — a relocation §1b's written text does not carry, since §1b deletes the reader and §2 rewrites it in scripts/ instead

findings.reason: naming extract_vessel_shells as the owner to extend gives the author one place to add the annular inner/outer reading instead of a second extractor that will drift from it.
findings.text: §4 adds a vessel field to MachineGeometry (imas_ink/_types.py:113) and draws it in geometry_figure_mpl (imas_ink/figures.py:138), forking the vessel-extraction owner that already exists as extract_vessel_shells (imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:151) with its VesselShell type (imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:43) and its description_2d.vessel.unit iteration; the plan should extend extract_vessel_shells (adding the outline_inner/outline_outer reading the annular vessel needs, which that owner currently omits) and reuse VesselShell in the geometry pipeline, rather than a second extractor and a second field shape beside it

findings.reason: the section must account for the public field it adds in its own text — naming the existing VesselShell it can reuse, or stating why the geometry pipeline cannot carry vessel contours through the type that already has them — before it is admitted.
findings.text: §4 states "It adds one field on MachineGeometry for the vessel contours" (and possibly a style constant) without naming what it retires or merges, and states no reason why nothing can be retired; the reuse that would retire the addition exists (VesselShell, imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:43), so the added field is avoidable public surface on MachineGeometry, against a week whose interface budget is public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0

duplicate_owner-1.reason: plan v28 §4 adds outline_inner/outline_outer reading to extract_vessel_shells (it reads only centreline+thickness or outline today) and carries VesselShell objects into the 2D geometry

interface_budget-1.reason: plan v28 §4 types the one MachineGeometry field with the existing VesselShell and states it retires nothing because the 2D geometry has no vessel representation today

reuse_search-1.reason: plan v28 §4 extends imas-ink's extract_vessel_shells and VesselShell instead of a new extractor; the §2 half is declined: §2 hands the IDSs to imas-ink's own extract_geometry, the extraction owner for its figure, and the stale landing comment about artifact_geometry described the retired reader

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the substantial behaviour is hidden behind imas-ink's geometry_figure_mpl and time_trace_figure_mpl; the ambix side is two thin scripts plus one reader (eddb.read_channel), which is a small surface over machinery rather than a spread of wrappers over it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 adds a second vessel-contour extractor beside imas-ink's existing owner of that extraction.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §4 adds a field on MachineGeometry (a public definition in the imas-ink API) without naming what it retires or merges, and the reuse that would let it retire the addition exists (VesselShell / extract_vessel_shells).
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites imas-ink's extract_geometry, geometry_figure_mpl, time_trace_figure_mpl and ambix's write_channel, but §4 proposes new vessel extraction without citing imas-ink's already-exported extract_vessel_shells (imas_ink/three_d/walls.py:151), and §2 rewrites a geometry reader whose own §1 landing comment names imas_ambix/gs/artifact_geometry.py as its home, a relocation that appears nowhere in §1b's design text.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 and §3 each add one thin script over imas-ink, and the figure-owner decision (imas-ink called from a thin ambix script, versus the rejected imas-ink CLI and nova media) states why the script is kept rather than the renderer extended; §3's read_channel carries its own justification for not reusing ZarrTransformEngine.read.
